result.summary: Checks for pending peer orphan transactions under m_tx_download_mutex before acquiring cs_main in ProcessOrphanTx. When a peer has no orphan transactions to reconsider, ProcessMessages returns early without locking cs_main. A test is added verifying that ProcessMessages completes without cs_main contention when no orphan work is pending.
result.problem: ProcessMessages calls ProcessOrphanTx for each connected peer on every loop pass (at least every 100 ms), acquiring cs_main unconditionally even when the peer has no orphan work. This causes the P2P message handler to unnecessarily block on validation, RPC, or wallet threads holding cs_main, delaying processing of unrelated messages such as pings.
evidence: Author benchmark: when another thread holds cs_main for 50 ms, handling a ping message in ProcessMessages drops from 50.1 ms on master to 0.02 ms with this change (PR description).
result.scope_notes: Small change (+38/-0 across 2 files) including a unit or functional test; the diff was omitted from the prompt.
result.card: Skips acquiring cs_main in ProcessOrphanTx when a peer has no orphan transactions queued, checking under m_tx_download_mutex first. Currently, ProcessMessages takes cs_main unconditionally for every peer on every message-handling pass, causing message processing to block on active validation or RPC operations. In author benchmarks with cs_main held for 50 ms, ping handling latency dropped from 50.1 ms to 0.02 ms. Intended to reduce lock contention independently while paving the way for asynchronous block processing in #36244.

risk.why: Incorrect locking or race conditions during orphan transaction reconsideration could lead to orphaned transactions being skipped or deadlocks between m_tx_download_mutex and cs_main.
